subject: Fix spurious jump-up step entry (f872 family)
description:
Re-diagnosis from fix-residuals (formula/duration exonerated — constants now exact): at linux2 P002/Savegame_002 replay-004 f872, Rust enters a REAL airborne JumpingUp (wait_time 1, Terminated first frame) while the Original's Pc 252 is completely IDLE frames 864-886 (constant position, posture 10→1 at 869, idle motion cycle). The bug is UPSTREAM: Rust's jump sequence advances into the airborne step at a moment the Original doesn't — step-entry/sequence timing. Related third signature: SuN Savegame_001 members f835/f778 show motion_state Aborted-vs-Terminated (another distinct cause).

ALSO in-scope: flight-increment rounding. SCOPING NOTES from fix-orderlag (not implemented):
- C++ ReadyForTakeOff (RHsprite.cpp, end of fn) computes the increment ONCE: `SetIncrement((ptRealGoal3D - ptMyPosition3D) / uwFramesOfFlight)`, and PerformFlight just adds the stored increment each frame.
- Rust advance_airborne_flight (engine/jump.rs:1870-1899) instead normalises the full vector each frame and multiplies by jump_airborne_speed(anim) (8/15/20). Per-frame delta therefore differs: C++ steps full_dist/frames, Rust steps the literal speed, so intermediate positions drift even when the endpoint snaps.
- The divisor already exists Rust-side: CurrentStepState.total_frames = sprite.total_ticks_for_anim(step.anim) (jump.rs:1498), which matches C++'s non-fall `uwFramesOfFlight = 1 + sum(GetWaitTime(row,i)+1)`.
- CAUTION: C++ picks uwFramesOfFlight differently per RHflightstyle — the FALL style uses `(ptMyPosition3D.mZ - ptRealGoal3D.mZ) / FALL_SPEED` and also sets muwFrameCountDown from it, while other styles use the animation duration. A faithful fix must reproduce that split, not just divide by total_frames everywhere. Rust's JumpingDown speed constant (20.0) is FALL_SPEED, so today's per-frame behaviour happens to be right only for a purely vertical fall.
resolution: Original retains one Execute-time airborne increment computed as delta * (speed / distance); Rust now stores and serializes that vector instead of renormalizing each tick. Final jump termination also mirrors Original's synchronous Ready/Instruct reset of the retained continuation motion state to InProgress. The primary linux2 schema-14 replay-004 reaches exact EOF. Archived SuN Aborted-vs-Terminated signatures contain no active jump and remain a separate generic MoveOk/WalkingWithSword completion family.
